questions.q: Without solving it, explain how you know $x^2+2x+5=0$ has complex (not real) roots.
questions.answer: Its discriminant is $\Delta=2^2-4(1)(5)=4-20=-16<0$. A negative discriminant means the quadratic formula takes the square root of a negative number, giving a complex conjugate pair (Theorem 1.1) instead of real roots.

questions.q: Verify that $x=-3+2i$ is a root of $x^2+6x+13=0$ by direct substitution.
Find $|z|$ for $z=-3+2i$ (one of the roots found above).
Explain why a conjugate pair $a\pm bi$ always has the same modulus for both roots.
questions.answer: $|a+bi|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ and $|a-bi|=\sqrt{a^2+(-b)^2}=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ — squaring $b$ or $-b$ gives the same result, so the two moduli are identical.
